module: UI navigation router on the Lua side (ui_router). It orchestrates a "handshake" with the UI frameworks (Vue, Angular/legacy): route resolution, exit/entry guards, lifecycle hooks (onLeave, onEnter, onMount), sending the route change to the framework, then receiving the acknowledgments (received, navigation started, route committed, mounted). It delegates state to the ui/router/* modules (navigationState, transitionManager, frameworkManager, guardManager, scopeManager, breadcrumbManager...). A modder mostly uses it to call navigate/back/reload and to listen to the onUiChangedState and onUiActiveScopeChanged hooks.
usage:
-- navigate to a route with parameters
local res = ui_router.navigate("mainmenu", {})
if not res.success then log("W", "mod", "failed: " .. tostring(res.reason)) end
-- non-cancellable navigation (protection lock)
ui_router.navigate("photomode", nil, {cancellable = false})
notes: Sequence of a navigation: 1) navigate emits the route change (FrameworkManager.sendRouteChange); 2) routeChangeReceived; 3) routeNavigationStarted; 4) routeChangeComplete promotes the pending entry and ends the transition, except for Vue routes which wait for a mount acknowledgment; 5) routeMounted runs onMount and ends the transition.
For Vue routes, the acknowledgments must return a non-empty transition identifier (otherwise reason="missing_transition_id"). Angular/legacy can do without it and are validated by route name.

A navigate with options.cancellable == false acquires a lock identified by a unique token ("navProtect_N") that blocks any following navigate/back/reload (reason="active_navigation_not_cancellable") until the terminal state of this navigation (end, cancellation, failure, timeout, reset, deserialization). Otherwise the last navigation wins and cancels the transition in progress (cancellation "navigation_replaced").

navigate failures return {result=false, success=false, reason=...}: active_navigation_not_cancellable, route_not_found, guard_blocked_exit, guard_blocked_enter, lifecycle_hook_error, navigation_preempted, or the route reference resolution error.
The route name accepts an enriched reference: relative route resolved against the current route, inline query (?a=1) and scope (:scope). Explicit parameters take precedence over those of the query.

Emitted hooks: extensions.hook(BEFORE_ROUTE_CHANGE, entry), AFTER_ROUTE_CHANGE, ROUTE_CHANGE_CANCELLED (toRoute, fromRoute, reason, transitionId, plus timeoutClassification/phase/... for a timeout), ROUTE_TIMING (routeName, {total, enter, ready, mountAcked} in ms), onUiChangedState(routeName, originRoute) and onUiActiveScopeChanged(payload). UI event: guihooks ui_router_routeData (namespace, route, fromRoute, scopeTree, scopeParentMap, targetScope, breadcrumbs, data, status, error) with status = enter-ready, mounted-ready or error.
NavigationObserver (diagnostic) is loaded only if shipping_build ~= true.
back() returns nothing (nil) if the current route has neither a backTarget nor a valid back handler.
The extension sets itself to manual unload on load (setExtensionUnloadMode manual) and reloads the guards (GuardManager.reloadGuards).
Deprecated functions: push, replace (log a warning then call navigate) and forward (returns {result=false, reason="deprecated_method"}). The __test_* functions are access points reserved for tests.

navigate.desc: Navigates to a route: resolves the target, runs the exit guards of the current route, cancels any transition in progress, runs onLeave, the entry guards, onEnter, emits the route data (status enter-ready) then starts the transition to the UI framework.

routename.desc: Route name, possibly relative, with inline query (?a=1) and scope (:scope).

params.desc: Route parameters (take precedence over the inline query parameters).

options.desc: Options: cancellable (false = protected navigation), decorator, showDecorator, restoreLastScope, routeScopeId (added automatically)... passed to the route request.

returns.desc: {result=true, success=true, data=entry} or {result=false, success=false, reason=string, failedGuard?}.

back.desc: Back: navigates to the current route's backTarget (with the parameters of the previous entry if it matches, otherwise those of the current route, and restoreLastScope = true); otherwise runs the declared back handler (RouteHandlers) if the mode is "handler".

options.desc: Navigation options copied into the back navigation.

returns.desc: Result of navigate or of the handler; {result=false, reason="no_current_route"} without a current route; nil if nothing to do.

cancel.desc: Cancels the transition in progress (reason "cancelled"): notifies the framework and emits the ROUTE_CHANGE_CANCELLED hook.

returns.desc: {success=true}, or {success=false, message} if there is no transition.

getCurrent.desc: Returns the current (committed) navigation entry from NavigationState.

returns.desc: Current entry {request, resolved, routeNode, ...} or nil.

reload.desc: Replays the navigation: reuses the name, parameters and options of the current entry for missing arguments, then calls navigate.

params.desc: Parameters (default: those of the current request).

options.desc: Options (default: those of the current request).

returns.desc: Result of navigate, or {success=false, message} if there is no route to reload.

getBreadcrumbs.desc: Returns the breadcrumb of the current route (NavigationState.getBreadcrumbs).

getState.desc: Returns the router state: the current route and the active scope state.

isNavigationProtected.desc: Indicates whether a protected navigation (cancellable = false) is active.

returns.desc: true if the protection lock is held.

resetStates.desc: Resets the whole router state: navigation, transition, observer (non-shipping), protection lock, route data and active scope.

reportActiveScope.desc: Called by the UI to report the active scope. Ignores reports from a stale route, stores the route's last active scope (excluding popups, and if the scope is declared in the tree) then emits the onUiActiveScopeChanged hook.

routeChangeReceived.desc: Framework acknowledgment: the route change was received. Marks the routeChangeReceived progress of the transition.

transitionId.desc: Transition identifier returned by the UI.

routeNavigationStarted.desc: Framework acknowledgment: navigation on the UI side has started. Requires a transition identifier for Vue during a transition.

routeChangeRejected.desc: Definitive rejection by the UI of an impossible or malformed route change (routes that are merely absent are not rejected because they may register later). Cancels the active transition if the identifier matches.

reason.desc: Rejection reason (diagnostic, passed to the hook).

routeChangeComplete.desc: Framework acknowledgment: the route is committed on the UI side. Promotes the pending entry to current entry, notifies the framework, emits the AFTER_ROUTE_CHANGE and onUiChangedState hooks, and ends the transition unless a Vue mount acknowledgment is expected (and onEnter did not fail).

routeName.desc: Committed route (must match the pending entry).

routeChangeFailed.desc: Navigation failure reported by the framework (for example a Vue component that cannot be loaded). Cancels the navigation in progress without touching the committed route: validates route and identifier, refuses if the route is already committed, runs the pending destination's onLeave to cancel the effects of its onEnter, then cancels the transition.

frameworkId.desc: Emitting framework (required with identifier for Vue).

routeMounted.desc: Vue acknowledgment: the route's component is mounted. Requires a transition identifier, a committed route (otherwise reason="not_committed"), runs onMount, emits the route data (status mounted-ready or error) and ends the transition. A late/duplicate acknowledgment for the already committed route returns {success=true, stale=true}.

onGuiUpdate.desc: Hook called on every GUI update (time arguments of the main loop): advances the TransitionManager, resends the route change message to the framework if needed (startup resends) or handles a transition timeout (emits the route data in error then cancels).

onSerialize.desc: Hook called before a Lua extensions reload: returns {navigation = NavigationState.serialize()}.

onDeserialize.desc: Hook called after a reload: clears the (stale) protection lock and restores NavigationState from data.navigation.

onExtensionLoaded.desc: Hook called when the extension is loaded: switches to manual unload and reloads the route guards.

push.desc: Deprecated: logs a warning and calls navigate.

replace.desc: Deprecated: logs a warning and calls navigate.

forward.desc: Deprecated and not implemented: always returns a failure.

__test_getProtectionToken.desc: Access point reserved for tests: returns the token of the protected navigation lock.

__test_setProtectionToken.desc: Access point reserved for tests: forces the token of the protected navigation lock.
